arxiv-2206-11241.title: Concentration inequalities and optimal number of layers for stochastic deep neural networks
arxiv-2206-11241.creator: Michele Caprio and Sayan Mukherjee
arxiv-2206-11241.description: Abstract . We state concentration inequalities for the output of the hidden layers of a stochastic deep neural network (SDNN), as well as for the output of the whole SDNN. These results allow us to introduce an expected classifier (EC), and to give probabilistic upper bound for the classification error of the EC.

arxiv-2206-14930.title: A multiscale thermodynamic generalization of Maxwell-Stefan diffusion equations and of the dusty gas model
arxiv-2206-14930.creator: Petr Vágner, Michal Pavelka, Jürgen Fuhrmann, Václav Klika
arxiv-2206-14930.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Petr Vágner, Michal Pavelka, Jürgen Fuhrmann, Václav Klika. Despite the fact that the theory of mixtures has been part of non-equilibrium thermodynamics and engineering for a long time, it is far from complete. While it is well formulated and tested in the case of mechanical equilibrium (where only diffusion-like processes take place), the question how to properly describe homogeneous mixtures that flow with multiple independent velocities that still possess some inertia (before mechanical equilibrium is reached) is still open.

arxiv-2305-18954.title: Poster: Towards Battery-Free Machine Learning Inference and Model Personalization on MCUs DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: The 21st ACM International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications, and Services; June 18–12, 2023; Helsinki, Finland Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 Conference: T
arxiv-2305-18954.creator: Yushan Huang, Hamed Haddadi
arxiv-2305-18954.description: Abstract . Machine learning (ML) is moving towards edge devices. However, ML models with high computational demands and energy consumption pose challenges for ML inference in resource-constrained environments, such as the deep sea. To address these challenges, we propose a battery-free ML inference and model personalization pipeline for microcontroller units (MCUs).

arxiv-2405-17556.title: Solving Probabilistic Verification Problems of Neural Networks using Branch and Bound
arxiv-2405-17556.creator: David Boetius, Stefan Leue, Tobias Sutter
arxiv-2405-17556.description: Abstract Probabilistic verification problems of neural networks are concerned with formally analysing the output distribution of a neural network under a probability distribution of the inputs. Examples of probabilistic verification problems include verifying the demographic parity fairness notion or quantifying the safety of a neural network.

arxiv-2507-08087.title: Quark flavors in hot and dense holographic QCD: setup and comparison to data Preprint: APCTP Pre2025 - 016
arxiv-2507-08087.creator: Matti Järvinen, Toshali Mitra
arxiv-2507-08087.description: Abstract We establish a flavor dependent holographic framework for hot and dense QCD. To this end, we generalize a class of bottom-up holographic models for QCD in the Veneziano limit (V-QCD) by incorporating explicit flavor dependence. Specifically, we develop a 2 + 1 2+1 flavor model characterized by two massless light quarks and a massive strange quark.

Subalgebras of upper triangular matrix algebras have played a fundamental role in the classification of minimal varieties of polynomial growth. Such classification has become a source of study in recent years since it leads to the more general classification of varieties of polynomial growth n k n^{k} , as has already been proven in many contexts for several values of k k .

pmc-10624773.title: Endophthalmitis caused by Burkholderia cepacia complex (BCC): clinical characteristics, antibiotic susceptibilities, and treatment outcomes
pmc-10624773.creator: Flavius A Beca, Jesse D Sengillo, Hailey K Robles-Holmes, Prashanth G Iyer, Darlene Miller, Nicolas A Yannuzzi, Harry W Flynn
pmc-10624773.description: PurposeTo report the clinical characteristics, antibiotic susceptibilities, and review the literature of Burkholderia cepacia complex (BCC) associated endophthalmitis.Study designRetrospective, observational case series.MethodsClinical and microbiology records were reviewed for patients evaluated at the Bascom Palmer Eye Institute and diagnosed wisth culture-confirmed endophthalmitis due to BCC. Antibiotic susceptibility profiles were generated using standard microbiologic protocols via an automated VITEK system.

pmc-10829444.title: “Is it time for personalised medicine for Ameloblastoma?”: A hypothesis
pmc-10829444.creator: Bhaskar Narayan, Somesh Kumar, Priya Kumar, Aadithya B. Urs
pmc-10829444.description: Ameloblastoma is a benign odontogenic tumor that is locally destructive. The most common treatment option is surgery, which often results in disfigurement of the face. BRAFV600E is the common gene mutation associated with its pathogenesis. Therefore, this paper hypothesizes the use of targeted drug therapy against this mutated gene.

pmc-11294551.title: Trends in hospital capacity and utilization in Puerto Rico by health regions, 2010–2020
pmc-11294551.creator: Jim P Stimpson, Alexandra C Rivera-González, Damaris Lopez Mercado, Jonathan Purtle, Glorisa Canino, Alexander N Ortega
pmc-11294551.description: Like many under resourced, island communities, most of the municipalities in Puerto Rico are medically underserved. However, there is limited information about changes in hospital capacity and any regional disparities in availability of hospital services in Puerto Rico, especially given the multiple public health emergencies the island has faced in recent years (e.g. hurricanes, earthquakes, and COVID-19).

pmc-12781799.title: Tropical cyclone activity predicts autumn vagrancy of Nearctic birds on a remote North Atlantic island
pmc-12781799.creator: David Monticelli
pmc-12781799.description: Wind drift has long been invoked as a primary driver of the seasonal appearance in Europe of long-distance migrants from North America (‘Nearctic vagrants’), presumed to be displaced beyond their normal range by westerly crosswinds and tropical storms encountered during migration. Yet few studies have tested how tropical cyclone (TC) activity shapes long-term patterns in offshore vagrancy.

pmc-13023294.title: New Diagnostic Score for Sepsis in Adult Horses with Acute Gastrointestinal Disease
pmc-13023294.creator: Angélique Blangy-Letheule, Jérôme Montnach, Julien Perrier, Louise C. Lemonnier, Manon Denis, Bertrand Rozec, Benjamin Lauzier, Aurélia A. Leroux
pmc-13023294.description: Simple SummaryColic is a common and serious digestive problem in adult horses that can become life-threatening when it causes widespread inflammation and organ failure. Recognizing when a horse develops a severe infection that leads to sepsis is difficult because no standard method exists.

pmc-13155753.title: Mettl5 coordinates protein production and degradation of PERIOD to regulate sleep in Drosophila
pmc-13155753.creator: Xiaoyu Wu, Xingzhuo Yang, Tiantian Fu, Yikang Rong, Juan Du, Jiwon Shim, Xiaoyu Wu, Xingzhuo Yang, Tiantian Fu, Yikang Rong, Juan Du
pmc-13155753.description: Sleep plays a critical role in animal physiology, primarily governed by the brain, and its disruption is prevalent in various brain disorders. Mettl5 is associated with intellectual disability (ID), which often includes sleep disturbances. However, the mechanism underlying these sleep disruptions in ID remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the sleep phenotypes resulting from Drosophila Mettl5 mutations.

pmc-13422806.description: ObjectivesThis paper constitutes an intervention development paper, illustrating the application of the person-based approach to planning and developing a digital transdiagnostic intervention to support Portuguese adults in managing their stress and emotions, thereby enhancing their mental health.DesignA multi-method intervention development study following the person-based approach (Phase I: collating and analysing evidence; Phase II: creating the intervention plan).

pmc-13434665.creator: Parisa Shirmohammadi, Fatemeh Fazeli, Alaleh Zoghi, Nasim Khorshidian, Mehrdad Mohammadi

This study evaluated the effects of adding S. platensis powder (0, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 3, and 5%) to pasta on cooking properties, color, hardness and sensory assessment. pmc-13587916.title: Implicitly tuned: The neural effects of social feedback on adolescent learning
pmc-13587916.creator: Alexis N Bosseler, Erica Peterson, Katherine K Meltzoff, Julia C Mizrahi, Eric Larson, Neva M Corrigan, Samu Taulu, Andrew N Meltzoff, Patricia K Kuhl
pmc-13587916.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Adolescents are particularly tuned to social cues, but how does this sensitivity affect their learning? This study examined whether social feedback conveyed through human faces modulates implicit learning of auditory speech patterns. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) was used to assess neural measures of learning in response to auditory linguistic input as participants engaged in a computer-controlled guessing task and received incidental social feedback in the form of smiling (positive) or frowning (negative) faces.

pmc-13633406.creator: Aqeel Abbas, Nouman Amjad, Amna Faheem Mufti, Muhammad Waqas, Minahil Iqbal, Hamza Ali, Amir Habib, Yahya Samadi, Muhammad Usman Haider

pmc-13634520.title: Cecal microbiota and metabolomic profiles associated with residual feed intake divergence in laying ducks
pmc-13634520.creator: N. Li, J. Yu, J-G. Wang, H. Shen, J. Wang
pmc-13634520.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Feed efficiency is an important determinant of productivity in laying ducks, but the cecal microbiota and metabolomic profiles associated with residual feed intake (RFI) divergence remain unclear. In this study, 767 laying ducks were phenotyped for RFI, and cecal samples from low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) ducks (n = 20 per group) were subjected to 16S rRNA gene sequencing and LC–MS-based untargeted metabolomics.
